screens.name: 01-today
screens.note: The paper on the step: masthead, dateline, the press turning, and the section line of the ten the desk has actually set for today.

screens.name: 02-question
screens.note: A pressed answer: the ink sweep landed, the stamp straddling the rule of the box she chose, the run struck out in pencil beside the tally, the correction circled, the footnote set.

screens.name: 03-result
screens.note: The edition printed: the score at 112pt, the tally, the tier stamp across three quarters of the page, the brass ribbon, and the line naming what is waiting above the clock.

screens.name: 04-scorecard
screens.note: The file: the run at 96pt over one ledger line, and the month printed in ink.

screens.name: 05-paywall
screens.note: Needs -fakeProducts: a scheme's StoreKit configuration is never honoured by a simctl launch, so real products are unavailable and the CTA would sit disabled.

screens.name: 06-practice
screens.note: The composing room, locked: the type case as its hero, the bullets as ruled lines.

screens.name: 07-onboarding
screens.note: The first screen anyone sees: the masthead over the drawn hand press.

screens.name: 08-settings
screens.note: The desk: sounds, what has been filed, and the attribution as the section footer.

screens.name: 09-share
screens.note: Not a screen of the app: the 1080x1350 front page the result shares, at the size it arrives in a chat. Nothing in the UI leads here — it is the only way to see the share image, since nothing on a runner can photograph a share sheet.

screens.name: 10-late-edition
screens.note: The one door money does not open: at seven editions filed the late edition arrives, set from the questions that got past her. -editions 12 is a reader who earned it five editions ago; nothing was purchased to reach this screen.

moments.name: answer
moments.note: The ink press: the app answers question four right at 6s, turns the page at 9s and answers question five wrong at 11.5s, so the sweep, the stamp, the tally, the pencil correction and the run being struck out are all on camera.

moments.name: win
moments.note: The edition printing: the tenth answer lands at 8s and the page goes to press at 12s, so the sheet, the press, the score counting up, the tier stamp and the burst are all inside the strip. A screenshot of a page that is animating hard costs two to three seconds on a runner, so the film is long and loose rather than tight — the 2.8s burst has to be wider than the gap between two frames to be caught at all.

ladder.name: edition-1
ladder.note: Rung 1: the section line prints the edition's make-up — four easy, four medium, two hard — and nothing is on record, so the desk deals the day's slate in the order the date sets.

ladder.name: edition-10
ladder.note: Rung 10: the mix has not moved yet — the first hard rung is at 39 — but ninety questions are on record and the sections are hers, not the calendar's.

ladder.name: edition-60
ladder.note: Rung 60: three easy, four medium, three hard, over a run of sixty in brass.

ladder.name: edition-200
ladder.note: Rung 200: one easy, three medium, six hard — the top of the ladder, and six hundred questions on record, so the sections on the line are the ones that keep catching her.
